column2: Development-ready starting taxonomy for category selection, AI classification, granular listing capture, faceted search and future pricing models.
Marketplace taxonomy for physical goods plus real-estate/property listings. Up to 3 category levels (L1/L2/L3). Jobs and standalone services remain excluded from this taxonomy.
39 L1 categories, 157 L2 groups, 907 L3 rows including long-tail catch-alls and real-estate property types.

Physical-goods listings inherit Common Metadata and a category-specific Metadata Profile. Real estate uses an asset-first hierarchy (Homes, New Developments, Land, Commercial, Shared Living) while Buy/Sell/Rent is captured separately as transaction intent.
Allowed = normal listing flow; Conditional = policy/compliance checks needed; Prohibited items are not represented as sellable categories and are listed on the Restrictions tab.
No finite taxonomy can literally enumerate every future item. "Other <L2>" catch-all nodes are included so unknown long-tail products can still be listed and reviewed for taxonomy promotion.

AI can propose L1/L2/L3 + extract metadata, but seller confirmation should remain authoritative for non-visible attributes such as age, warranty, working status, ownership, repair history and authenticity.
Index common metadata plus category profile facets in OpenSearch. Keep dynamic category-specific attributes in a schema-driven attribute model rather than adding database columns for every field.

Use category + metadata to retrieve comparables. For property, use transaction intent, locality, area, configuration, availability and property attributes. Do not rely on image AI alone to estimate item or property price.

Category Taxonomy columns L:O are provisional design guidance only. "Likely Eligible" means a plausible parcel-delivery candidate; "Conditional / Partner Check" means shipping constraints such as size, weight, battery, liquid, fragility, high value or policy must be validated; "Not Delivery Eligible" is used for non-parcel asset classes such as real estate and whole vehicles. Production UI must ultimately read a partner-confirmed DB flag at L3/category level plus runtime serviceability checks; do not hard-code these provisional values.

Category Taxonomy columns P:S are provisional launch-time UI controls. Show only enabled categories. At L1, display up to 15 categories flagged Yes, ordered by L1 UI Rank, then an Others control for remaining enabled L1 categories. Within an L1, display up to 10 L2 categories flagged Yes, ordered by L2 UI Rank, then Others for the remaining enabled L2 categories. Popularity should later be tuned from search, listing, click-through and transaction analytics.

Category Taxonomy columns T:V provide initial Admin Enabled flags for L1, L2 and L3. All are Yes initially. Parent disablement should override descendants in runtime UI/search/listing flows. The taxonomy sheet is denormalized, so L1/L2 flags repeat across descendant rows; in the production category table, store the flag once per category node.
